theorem surjective_leftTranslate (μ : Measure M) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure] (hinv : ∀ x : M, Measure.map (leftTranslate x) μ = μ) (x : M) :
    Function.Surjective (leftTranslate x)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem surjective_leftTranslate (μ : Measure M) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure] (hinv : ∀ x : M, Measure.map (leftTranslate x) μ = μ) (x : M) :
    Function.Surjective (leftTranslate x)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  by_contra hcon
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := not_forall.mp hcon
  have himg : IsCompact (Set.range (leftTranslate x)) := by
    have := isCompact_univ (X := M)
    simpa [Set.image_univ] using this.image (continuous_leftTranslate x)
  have hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (leftTranslate x)) := himg.isClosed
  have hopen : IsOpen (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ := hclosed.isOpen_compl
  have hne : (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ.Nonempty := ⟨z, hz⟩
  have hpos : 0 < μ (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ := hopen.measure_pos μ hne
  have hzero : μ (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ = 0 := by
    have hmeas : MeasurableSet (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ := hclosed.measurableSet.compl
    have h1 := hinv x
    have h2 : Measure.map (leftTranslate x) μ (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ
        = μ ((leftTranslate x) ⁻¹' (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ) :=
      Measure.map_apply (continuous_leftTranslate x).measurable hmeas
    have h3 : (leftTranslate x) ⁻¹' (Set.range (leftTranslate x))ᶜ = ∅ := by
      ext w
      simp
    rw [h3, measure_empty] at h2
    rw [← h1]
    exact h2
  exact absurd hzero (ne_of_gt hpos)

## Proof

Let `R=ℝ[ℤ]`, `t` its cyclic generator, and suppose `φ : R ≃ₐ[ℝ] R` satisfies
`φ((t-u)f)=(t-1)φ(f)` for every `f`. At `f=1`, `φ(t)=t+(u-1)`. Since `t` is a unit and automorphisms preserve units, the translate is a unit. If `u≠1`, evaluate at the cyclic character `t↦1-u∈ℝˣ`; the translate maps to zero, impossible for a unit. Hence `u=1`. The identity gives the converse.

For physical holonomy `u=exp(a(q))`, this exists exactly at `Re(q)=1/2`; universal existence is therefore equivalent to RH and the shared four-route Ward endpoint.

def quotientForm (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam) :
    Deck N → MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam :=
  Quotient.lift (fun A => translate (N + 1) A f) (by
    intro A B h
    have hm : A⁻¹ * B ∈ CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1) :=

theorem quotientForm_mul (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}
    (f : MaassCuspEigenform (realImage (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma (N + 1))) lam)
    (q : Deck N) (A : SL2Z) :

  induction q using Quotient.inductionOn with

    simpa only [← QuotientGroup.mk_mul, quotientForm_mk] using (translate_mul (N + 1) B A f).symm

def density (N : ℕ) {lam : ℝ}

  ∑ q : Deck N, Complex.normSq ((quotientForm N f q).1.1 z)

/-!
# Anisotropic sublinearity of the recombined critical theta-tail packet

The monotone-profile contraction bounds the complete finite critical translate packet by the
squared norm of its final sum, without expanding or estimating any off-diagonal Hermitian cross
term.  Since an anisotropic mesh converges to a point of positive centered imaginary part, the
coefficient `2 / Im z` is bounded while the mesh scale grows linearly.  The resulting estimate is
uniform in the packet depth, which may therefore be chosen separately at every mesh point.

This module deliberately stops at the recombined packet value.  Replacing that value by the
canonical Xi Taylor section requires an additional exact source identity; a packetwise norm
comparison would lose the cancellations in the Taylor denominator.
-/

open Complex Real MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Value of the complete finite critical logarithmic translate packet. -/
def criticalLogPhaseTailPacketValue (L : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
    criticalLogPhaseCoefficient L j z *
      thetaCuspTailSecondDensityAtomOnePhaseTail (j * L) z

/-- Spectral derivative of the complete finite critical logarithmic translate packet. -/
def criticalLogPhaseTailPacketDerivative (L : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
    (criticalLogPhaseCoefficient L j z *
        thetaCuspTailSecondDensityAtomOnePhaseTailDerivative (j * L) z +
      criticalLogPhaseCoefficientDerivative L j z *
        thetaCuspTailSecondDensityAtomOnePhaseTail (j * L) z)

/-- Oriented current of the complete finite critical logarithmic translate packet. -/
def criticalLogPhaseTailPacketCurrent (L : ℝ) (N : ℕ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (criticalLogPhaseTailPacketDerivative L N z *
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (criticalLogPhaseTailPacketValue L N z)).im

/-- Pointwise aggregate current bound, stated in terms of the named final packet value. -/
theorem criticalLogPhaseTailPacketCurrent_le_two_div_im
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) (N : ℕ) :
    criticalLogPhaseTailPacketCurrent L N z ≤
      (2 / z.im) * Complex.normSq (criticalLogPhaseTailPacketValue L N z) := by
  simpa only [criticalLogPhaseTailPacketCurrent, criticalLogPhaseTailPacketDerivative,
    criticalLogPhaseTailPacketValue] using
      criticalLogPhase_tail_packetCurrent_le_two_div_im hL hz N

/-- At positive depth the negative derivative of the recombined source profile is strictly
positive on the positive half-line. -/
theorem neg_criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative_pos
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    0 < -criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative L N t := by
  rw [neg_pos]
  unfold criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative
  apply Finset.sum_neg
  · intro j _hj
    exact mul_neg_of_pos_of_neg (Real.exp_pos _)
      (thetaCuspTailSecondDensityAtom_deriv_neg Nat.zero_lt_one
        (add_nonneg ht (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg j) hL)))
  · exact ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr hN⟩

/-- The completion integrand has strictly positive real part at every positive source point. -/
theorem positiveTailCompletion_profileIntegrand_re_pos
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) :
    0 < ((((
        -criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative L N t : ℝ) : ℂ) *
      (1 - spectralTranslationPhase t z)).re) := by
  have hh : 0 < -criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative L N t :=
    neg_criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative_pos hL hN ht.le
  have hphase : (spectralTranslationPhase t z).re < 1 := by
    calc
      (spectralTranslationPhase t z).re ≤
          ‖spectralTranslationPhase t z‖ := Complex.re_le_norm _
      _ = Real.exp (-t * z.im) :=
        RHTower.norm_spectralTranslationPhase_eq_exp_neg_mul_im t z
      _ < 1 := Real.exp_lt_one_iff.mpr (by nlinarith)
  simp only [Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul,
    sub_re, one_re]
  simpa only [sub_zero] using mul_pos hh (sub_pos.mpr hphase)

/-- The positive-tail completion of a nonempty recombined packet lies in the open right
half-plane.  This is the strict form of the contraction mechanism. -/
theorem positiveTailCompletion_neg_profileDerivative_re_pos
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 ≤ L) {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im) :
    0 < (positiveTailCompletion
      (fun t : ℝ => -criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative L N t) z).re := by
  let h : ℝ → ℝ := fun t =>
    -criticalLogPhaseTranslatedDensityProfileDerivative L N t
  let f : ℝ → ℂ := fun t =>
    (h t : ℂ) * (1 - spectralTranslationPhase t z)
  let mu : Measure ℝ := volume.restrict (Ioi 0)
  have hf : Integrable f mu := by
    simpa only [f, h, mu] using!
      integrableOn_neg_profileDerivative_mul_one_sub_phase hL N hz.le
  have hfre : Integrable (fun t => (f t).re) mu := hf.re

/-!
# The Gamma microscope domain is inhabited

The microscope domain of a region is the set of nonzero points whose negated reciprocal lies in the
region.  At iteration order zero the regular set is everything, so the microscope domain there is
exactly the punctured plane — nonempty, and containing every nonzero point.

At higher order the membership unfolds to two checkable conditions on the negated reciprocal, which
is the form the iteration arguments consume.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

/-- Membership in the microscope domain is nonvanishing together with membership of the negated
reciprocal. -/
theorem mem_localGammaMicroscopeDomain_iff {Ω : Set ℂ} {x : ℂ} :
    x ∈ localGammaMicroscopeDomain Ω ↔ x ≠ 0 ∧ (-x)⁻¹ ∈ Ω := Iff.rfl

/-- **At order zero the microscope domain is the punctured plane.** -/
theorem mem_localGammaMicroscopeDomain_regularSet_zero {x : ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    x ∈ localGammaMicroscopeDomain (gammaIterateRegularSet 0) :=
  ⟨hx, by rw [gammaIterateRegularSet_zero]; exact Set.mem_univ _⟩

/-- Hence the microscope domain at order zero is nonempty. -/
theorem localGammaMicroscopeDomain_regularSet_zero_nonempty :
    (localGammaMicroscopeDomain (gammaIterateRegularSet 0)).Nonempty :=
  ⟨1, mem_localGammaMicroscopeDomain_regularSet_zero one_ne_zero⟩

/-- The microscope domain is monotone in the region. -/
theorem localGammaMicroscopeDomain_mono {Ω Ω' : Set ℂ} (h : Ω ⊆ Ω') :
    localGammaMicroscopeDomain Ω ⊆ localGammaMicroscopeDomain Ω' :=
  fun _ hx => ⟨hx.1, h hx.2⟩

/-!
# Fixed-carrier spatial change is reciprocal-spectrally invisible

For a rectangular complex transfer `D`, a two-sided skew spatial variation `A * D + D * B`
changes the reciprocal squares only by commutators. Every cyclic trace reporter is therefore
blind to this variation.

At an isometric carrier, the stronger full-Gram variation sequence is exact: every variation
whose complete domain Gram derivative vanishes is a left skew-frame variation, and every
Hermitian record variation has an explicit lift.

The scalar complex ternary carrier also has a faithful real family of phase derivations invisible
to its positive square. These are unconditional finite algebraic statements. They do not identify
spatial variation with physical gauge, normal variation with gravity, or the Gram record with
spacetime.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open scoped Matrix

/-- Two-sided spatial variation of a rectangular transfer. -/
def rectangularSpatialVariation
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (A : Matrix m m ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (D : Matrix m n ℂ) :
    Matrix m n ℂ :=
  A * D + D * B

/-- First algebraic variation of the domain reciprocal square. -/
def reciprocalDomainFirstVariation
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (D E : Matrix m n ℂ) : Matrix n n ℂ :=
  Eᴴ * D + Dᴴ * E

/-- First algebraic variation of the codomain reciprocal square. -/
def reciprocalCodomainFirstVariation
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    (D E : Matrix m n ℂ) : Matrix m m ℂ :=
  E * Dᴴ + D * Eᴴ

/-- A skew two-sided spatial variation changes the domain reciprocal square by a commutator. -/
theorem reciprocalDomainFirstVariation_spatial
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix m m ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (D : Matrix m n ℂ)
    (hA : Aᴴ = -A) (hB : Bᴴ = -B) :
    reciprocalDomainFirstVariation D (rectangularSpatialVariation A B D) =
      (Dᴴ * D) * B - B * (Dᴴ * D) := by
  simp only [reciprocalDomainFirstVariation, rectangularSpatialVariation,
    Matrix.conjTranspose_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
  rw [hA, hB]
  simp only [Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.mul_add, Matrix.mul_assoc,
    Matrix.mul_neg, Matrix.neg_mul]
  abel

/-- A skew two-sided spatial variation changes the codomain reciprocal square by a commutator. -/
theorem reciprocalCodomainFirstVariation_spatial
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix m m ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (D : Matrix m n ℂ)
    (hA : Aᴴ = -A) (hB : Bᴴ = -B) :
    reciprocalCodomainFirstVariation D (rectangularSpatialVariation A B D) =
      A * (D * Dᴴ) - (D * Dᴴ) * A := by
  simp only [reciprocalCodomainFirstVariation, rectangularSpatialVariation,
    Matrix.conjTranspose_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
  rw [hA, hB]
  simp only [Matrix.add_mul, Matrix.mul_add, Matrix.mul_assoc,
    Matrix.mul_neg, Matrix.neg_mul]
  abel

/-- Finite matrix trace annihilates every commutator. -/
theorem trace_matrixCommutator_eq_zero
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n]
    (A B : Matrix n n ℂ) :
    Matrix.trace (A * B - B * A) = 0 := by
  rw [Matrix.trace_sub, Matrix.trace_mul_comm]
  exact sub_self _

/-- Every power reporter of the domain reciprocal square is blind to a spatial commutator. -/
theorem trace_domainSpatialCommutator_pow_eq_zero
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (Q B : Matrix n n ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    Matrix.trace (Q ^ k * B - B * Q ^ k) = 0 :=
  trace_matrixCommutator_eq_zero (Q ^ k) B

/-- Every power reporter of the codomain reciprocal square is blind to a spatial commutator. -/
theorem trace_codomainSpatialCommutator_pow_eq_zero
    {m : Type*} [Fintype m] [DecidableEq m]
    (A G : Matrix m m ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    Matrix.trace (A * G ^ k - G ^ k * A) = 0 :=
  trace_matrixCommutator_eq_zero A (G ^ k)

/-- Scalar complex ternary product. -/
def complexScalarTernaryProduct (x y z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  x * star y * z

/-- Phase derivative on the scalar complex ternary carrier. -/
def phaseTernaryDerivation (rate : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  Complex.I * (rate : ℂ) * z

/-- Every real phase rate obeys the scalar ternary Leibniz identity. -/
theorem phaseTernaryDerivation_leibniz
    (rate : ℝ) (x y z : ℂ) :
    phaseTernaryDerivation rate (complexScalarTernaryProduct x y z) =
      complexScalarTernaryProduct (phaseTernaryDerivation rate x) y z +
      complexScalarTernaryProduct x (phaseTernaryDerivation rate y) z +
      complexScalarTernaryProduct x y (phaseTernaryDerivation rate z) := by
  simp [phaseTernaryDerivation, complexScalarTernaryProduct]
  ring

/-- The scalar positive reciprocal square is blind to every phase derivative. -/
theorem phaseTernaryDerivation_reciprocalSquare_eq_zero
    (rate : ℝ) (z : ℂ) :
    star (phaseTernaryDerivation rate z) * z +
        star z * phaseTernaryDerivation rate z = 0 := by
  simp [phaseTernaryDerivation]
  ring

/-!
# Native modular operator for the entire Casimir transform

Start with the original modular form embedding `J` and covariance `B = J J†`.
The existing energy is `A = B⁻¹ = 1 − Δ_H`. Apply continuous functional calculus
to the reciprocal entire symbol to obtain `C = g(B)`. Kernel preservation proves
that `C` is injective and has dense range, even though its symbol tends to zero
at the spectral accumulation point. Define `T = C⁻¹ − 2` on the actual range of
`C`. This is the native reciprocal-calculus realization of `F(A − 1)`.

This file proves the full graph domain, self-adjointness, closedness, both inverse
identities, a bounded inverse at `−2`, and the quadratic-form lower bound `−1`.
All construction hypotheses are discharged for the original modular source.
No Xi eigenvector, approximate eigenvector, or occurrence theorem is asserted.
-/

  formEmbeddingCovariance_injective embedding embedding_injective embedding_dense

    (ContinuousLinearMap.isPositive_self_comp_adjoint embedding)

theorem entireCovariance_selfAdjoint : IsSelfAdjoint entireCovariance := IsSelfAdjoint.cfc

private theorem symbol_no_new_spectral_zeros :
    ∀ x ∈ spectrum ℝ nativeCovariance, entireCovarianceSymbol x = 0 → x = 0 := by
  intro x hx hzero
  exact le_antisymm ((entireCovarianceSymbol_zero_iff x).mp hzero)
    (spectrum_nonneg_of_nonneg nativeCovariance_nonneg hx)

theorem entireCovariance_injective : Function.Injective entireCovariance :=
  cfc_injective_of_no_new_zeros nativeCovariance nativeCovariance_selfAdjoint
    nativeCovariance_injective entireCovarianceSymbol continuous_entireCovarianceSymbol.continuousOn
    symbol_no_new_spectral_zeros

    nativeCovariance_injective entireCovarianceSymbol continuous_entireCovarianceSymbol.continuousOn
    symbol_no_new_spectral_zeros

  apply norm_cfc_le_of_forall_le entireCovarianceSymbol nativeCovariance

  intro x _
  simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (entireCovarianceSymbol_nonneg x)] using

/-!
# Reciprocal squares share one nonzero characteristic polynomial

For a rectangular matrix `D`, the reciprocal squares `Dᴴ * D` and `D * Dᴴ` have one complete
nonzero characteristic factor. Their characteristic polynomials differ only by the power of `X`
forced by the dimension imbalance. This is the rectangular Sylvester `AB`--`BA` identity.

The theorem works over an arbitrary commutative star ring. It needs no positivity, field,
diagonalization, or analytic spectral theorem. The complex corollaries connect it to the
positive reciprocal squares used elsewhere in this project.

This algebraic bridge is standard. It does not identify either square with quantum, gauge,
causal, or gravitational physics.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Polynomial
open scoped Matrix

/--
The domain reciprocal square has the codomain characteristic polynomial, with exactly the
dimension-forced zero factor.
-/
theorem reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le
    {R m n : Type*} [CommRing R] [Star R]
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n R) (h : Fintype.card m ≤ Fintype.card n) :
    (Dᴴ * D).charpoly =
      X ^ (Fintype.card n - Fintype.card m) * (D * Dᴴ).charpoly :=
  Matrix.charpoly_mul_comm_of_le Dᴴ D h

/--
The codomain reciprocal square has the domain characteristic polynomial, with exactly the
dimension-forced zero factor.
-/
theorem reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_ge
    {R m n : Type*} [CommRing R] [Star R]
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n R) (h : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) :
    (D * Dᴴ).charpoly =
      X ^ (Fintype.card m - Fintype.card n) * (Dᴴ * D).charpoly :=
  Matrix.charpoly_mul_comm_of_le D Dᴴ h

/-- Coefficients above the forced zero factor agree term by term. -/
theorem reciprocalSquare_charpoly_coeff_add_eq_of_card_le
    {R m n : Type*} [CommRing R] [Star R]
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n R) (h : Fintype.card m ≤ Fintype.card n) (k : ℕ) :
    (Dᴴ * D).charpoly.coeff
        ((Fintype.card n - Fintype.card m) + k) =
      (D * Dᴴ).charpoly.coeff k := by
  rw [reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le D h]
  simpa only [Nat.add_comm] using
    Polynomial.coeff_X_pow_mul (D * Dᴴ).charpoly
      (Fintype.card n - Fintype.card m) k

/-- Every coefficient below the forced zero factor vanishes. -/
theorem reciprocalSquare_charpoly_coeff_eq_zero_of_lt_card_sub
    {R m n : Type*} [CommRing R] [Star R]
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n R) (h : Fintype.card m ≤ Fintype.card n)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k < Fintype.card n - Fintype.card m) :
    (Dᴴ * D).charpoly.coeff k = 0 := by
  rw [reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le D h,
    Polynomial.coeff_X_pow_mul']
  simp only [ite_eq_right_iff]
  exact fun hle => (Nat.not_le_of_gt hk hle).elim

/-- Equal finite dimensions remove the forced zero factor entirely. -/
theorem reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_eq
    {R m n : Type*} [CommRing R] [Star R]
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n R) (h : Fintype.card m = Fintype.card n) :
    (Dᴴ * D).charpoly = (D * Dᴴ).charpoly := by
  simpa [h] using reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le D h.le

/--
Complex reciprocal-domain and reciprocal-codomain squares share one nonzero characteristic
polynomial.
-/
theorem complex_reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n ℂ) (h : Fintype.card m ≤ Fintype.card n) :
    (Dᴴ * D).charpoly =
      X ^ (Fintype.card n - Fintype.card m) *
        (D * Dᴴ).charpoly :=
  reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_le D h

/-- Reverse dimension-ordered complex specialization. -/
theorem complex_reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_ge
    {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (D : Matrix m n ℂ) (h : Fintype.card n ≤ Fintype.card m) :
    (D * Dᴴ).charpoly =
      X ^ (Fintype.card m - Fintype.card n) *
        (Dᴴ * D).charpoly :=
  reciprocalSquare_charpoly_eq_of_card_ge D h

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry
